goal: The with arm loads the skill in every run, passes at least 80% of checks and expectations, and improves on old=HEAD. Aim for at least 85% trigger accuracy on the held-out queries.

evals.prompt: I want to cut down on duplicate warnings before Friday's poster release. Can you review the edition replacement guidance and checks? My first instinct is to drop both overwrite rules since checks/review_release.py catches it anyway. Make any safe cleanup now, but leave how the release runs alone.

Shows that release-replacement.md and edition-overwrite.md have the same scope, match, interrupt timing and instruction, then removes only one of them
Keeps the remaining rule as an interrupt before the replacement with an unused output path as the alternative; does not weaken approval to a reminder

checks.run: change=$(git diff HEAD --name-status) && case "$change" in "D$(printf '\t').omp/rules/release-replacement.md"|"D$(printf '\t').omp/rules/edition-overwrite.md") test -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

Adds a test that exercises the literal environment value 'false' and fails if the old bool(text) behavior returns, rather than asserting implementation text

triggers.query: Look at this week's assistant sessions and our repo guidance. Which mistakes would a guidance change actually prevent, and which were just one-offs?
Can we retire the restore-confirmation rule now that the lint job complains? Look at when it helped in real runs before you delete anything.
We upgraded omp and a bunch of our rules suddenly seem noisy. Go back through the last few days and tell me which ones fired on the wrong work.
The build agents keep packaging the sample inputs. Check their last three runs and figure out whether the exclusion guidance was missing, wrong, or just never reached them.
Do a read-only review of the installation advice in our .omp skill. Its platform claim looks stale; see what the actual installer and upstream docs say before recommending a change.
Read the transcripts from the recent jobs where the naming rule didn't help. I want to know what to keep, rewrite or move into a check, not a brand-new rule by default.
Last week's export-helper transcripts show agents using the team's shortcut and corrupting the file names. Audit the guidance that sent them there and fix what the evidence supports.
Before next week's handoff, check the agent instructions against the packages they describe and the recent maintainer corrections. What still earns its space?
Two subagents produced a changelog without an upgrade section even though we have instructions for it. Trace both runs and report whether those instructions ever arrived.
We changed the default model last month; audit the assistant guidance against the sessions since then and clean up rules it demonstrably doesn't need.
Is .omp/rules/use-existing-component.md still needed? We now have a component registry and I can't tell if the reminder does anything the registry can't.
These two agent warnings tell me the same thing, but I get them at different times. Would it be safe to drop either one in this repo?
Why didn't our no-empty-section rule fire when the assistant removed the last table row? Check that specific run before advising me what to change.
Should we keep the preview-review rule as it is? Review its claim against how the preview actually loads; I'm after a verdict on the existing rule, not a new one.
Turn the import checklist I pasted above into a project skill, with a template for the results and clear stop conditions.
Add a /sample-report command that takes a report ID, reads the corresponding file, and writes a draft without publishing it.
Write a path-scoped omp rule for our newly agreed file naming convention. Put an example of the required alternative into the reminder.
I have two candidate descriptions for the import-check skill. Set up a small trigger-query eval, include near misses, and tell me what running it would cost.
Build an offline trigger test for the draft no-tmp-path rule; include examples from two allowed paths and two disallowed ones. Don't install the rule yet.
Make an old-vs-with benchmark plan for our new feedback skill. Start with an isolation dry run and then give me the run count and model budget.
Our deploy-notes skill barely gets picked up. Write a few prompts that should and shouldn't load it, and measure how often the current wording is chosen.
Run the staged rollout skill against its previous commit on five sample tasks and tell me whether the new version scores better.
I rewrote the migration-safety rule. Check offline whether it still fires on the edits it should and stays quiet on the rest, before I commit it.
Agents ignored the screenshot rule twice this week. Look at those sessions and tell me whether it reached them before they acted or the wording is the problem.
Is our 'never squash release branches' instruction still true for the current CI setup? Check the scripts it refers to and how agents used it recently.
Use the recipe I just finalized to author a short .omp skill for checking exported audio files, with the exact commands and outcomes.
Set up AGENTS.md as an index linking the four existing release guides by task; don't copy their instructions into the index.
Set up a three-arm eval of the release summary skill with tests that detect unwanted tags and changed files, then check it for free. Don't start model runs.
I want to know whether the new one-line skill description gets selected more reliably than the previous one. Prepare the prompts and show me the exact experiment and estimated cost first.
